harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created and enabled a systemd service `inventory-worker` on node1 that runs a long-running heartbeat loop, hardened with NoNewPrivileges=true, ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome=true, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory (plus PrivateTmp/PrivateDevices/CapabilityBoundingSet= etc.), running as a dedicated unprivileged system user. Confirmed confinement empirically (write outside /var/lib/inventory fails with the sandbox applied, write inside succeeds) and completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id, issued a native reboot, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified the service re-enabled itself, resumed as 'active/running' with the same hardening settings, and continued appending to /var/lib/inventory/inventory.log with data from before the restart intact.
actions_performed: Created /var/lib/inventory owned by new system user inventory-worker
Wrote /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh heartbeat loop
Wrote and enabled /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service with sandboxing directives (NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, etc.)
Started service and verified it was active/enabled and writing heartbeats
Ran systemd-run confinement tests: write outside /var/lib/inventory denied, write inside allowed
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service/data state on node1
Issued native reboot on node1 (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec was reachable again
Verified boot_id changed confirming an actual restart
Verified inventory-worker service auto-started post-boot with hardening intact and data/log continuity

evidence.summary: Service enabled+active immediately after creation; systemctl show confirms NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory; log file being written under /var/lib/inventory
systemd-run using the identical sandbox settings shows writing to /etc fails (exit 2, file never created) while writing inside /var/lib/inventory succeeds
Captured boot_id=96c08b66-... , uptime since original boot, service active/enabled, and current inventory.log contents before restart
Backgrounded native reboot command returned acknowledgement before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity / restart proof
evidence.summary: Connection reset confirms node went down; subsequent poll succeeds with a new boot_id (29b72a4e-...) differing from baseline and a fresh uptime start time, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: post-restart recovery of inventory-worker service and data
evidence.summary: After restart, service is active/running/enabled with identical hardening settings, prior log entries preserved, and new heartbeats (new PID 649) being appended, confirming full recovery
